item.title: Todoroki Valley — Guide
item.description: Todoroki Valley (Todoroki Keikoku), in Tokyo’s Setagaya ward, is a remarkable surprise: the city’s only natural ravine, a cool, leafy gorge carved by the Yazawa River that feels a world away from the surrounding suburbs. A pleasant walking path of around 1 km follows the small stream along the valley floor, shaded by dense greenery, crossed by little bridges, and lined with lush ferns and trees, offering a refreshingly cool escape especially in summer.

item.title: Philosopher's Path Guide: Kyoto's Most Beautiful Walk
item.description: The Philosopher’s Path (Tetsugaku-no-michi) is a stone-paved walking trail that follows a cherry-tree-lined canal through the quiet temple district of eastern Kyoto. Named for a famous philosophy professor who walked it daily in meditation on his way to Kyoto University, it strings together some of the city’s loveliest temples, shrines, cafés, and craft shops over about two gentle kilometres. In cherry-blossom season it becomes a tunnel of pink reflected in the water; in autumn, a corridor of red and gold.
